No embryo is developed in them."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"""All the organisms in the mentioned stem are taxonomically different from each other""- Discuss with logic.","marks":4,"answer":"The organisms mentioned in the stem are \textit{Paramecium}, \textit{yeast} and \textit{lion} which are part of the kingdoms Protista, Fungi and Animalia respectively. Taxonomically, they are quite different from each other since, they have different characteristics.
\textit{Paramecium} is part of the kingdom Protista which are unicellular or multicellular, individual or colonial or filamentous and the nuclei in their cells are well structured. Their cells contain nuclear materials bounded by a nuclear membrane. In chromatin material, there are DNA, RNA, and protein. All types of cell organelles are there in their cells. Their modes of nutrition are absorption, ingestion or photosynthesis. They accomplish their asexual and sexual reproduction by the process of mitosis and conjugation respectively. No embryo is developed in them.
\textit{Yeast} is part of kingdom Fungi which are mostly terrestrial, saprophytic or parasitic. Their body is constituted with a single cell or mycelium. Nucleus is well organized. Cell wall is composed of chitin. Their mode of nutrition is absorption. The photosynthetic apparatus chloroplast is absent in them. They reproduce by haploid spores. Their cells divide through mitotic cell division.
\textit{Lion} is part of Animalia kingdom that is characterized by heterotrophic eukaryotic organisms that are multicellular and their cells lack cell walls. They directly or indirectly depend on plants for food. They digest their food in an internal cavity and store food reserves as glycogen or fat. Their mode of nutrition is holozoic - by ingestion of food. They follow a definite growth pattern and grow into adults that have a definite shape and size. Higher forms show elaborate sensory and neuromotor mechanisms. The sexual reproduction is by copulation of male and female followed by embryological development.
Hence, the organisms has its own unique traits, they are classified in different taxa, in other words, they are taxonomically different from each other.
---"}]

It follows the unique two parts naming system called the binomial nomenclature. The rules are as follows-
i. The name has to have Latin word(s)
ii. The name has to have two parts; the first part is called genus and the following part is called species.
iii. The first letter of the first part of the scientific name has to be in capital letters, and rest of the letters including the first letter of the second part will be in small letters.
iv. Genus and species should be underlined separately. For example- \underline{Labeo\ rohita}

(Here L. is the short form of Linnaeus)"},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze the comparison among kingdom of the organisms of the stem.","marks":4,"answer":"The organisms mentioned in the stem are mushrooms, strawberries and Rui which belong to the kingdoms Fungi, Plantae and Animalia respectively. The kingdoms are compared below:
Fungi is usually terrestrial, saprophytic or parasitic. Plantae is photosynthetic and can produce it's own food. Animalia is characterized by heterotrophic eukaryotic organisms.
The body of Fungi is constituted with a single cell or mycelium. Their nucleus is well organized. Cell wall is composed of chitin. In plantae, advanced tissue systems are found. They develop embryots. They can be both ferrestrial and aquatic. Animals of Animalia are multicellular and their cells lack cell walls.
The mode of nutrition of Fungi is absorption. The photosynthetic apparatus chloroplast is absent in them. Plantae can prepare its' own food through the process of photosynthesis. Animals of Animalia directly or indirectly depend on plants for food. They digest their food in an internal cavity and store food reserves as glycogen or fat. Their mode of nutrition is holozoic.
Fungi reproduce by haploid spores. Their cells divide through mitotic cell division. The sexual reproduction of plantae is anisogamous. They are archegoniate and flowering plants. In Animalia, the sexual reproduction is by copulation of male and female followed by embryological development.

On the other hand, jute belongs to the kingdom plantae of the super kingdom eukaryota. They are photosynthetic and eukaryotic. Advanced tissue systems are found in them. They develop embryos and diploid stage is started from it. They are mostly terrestrial but there are also many aquatic species under this kingdom. Their sexual reproduction is of anisogamous type. Analyse with reasons.","marks":4,"answer":"Figure-E of the stem is \textit{Nostoc} (Monera) and Figure-F of the stem is Diatom (Protista). Among them, organisms belonging to the kingdom Protista (F) are more advanced than those belonging to the kingdom Monera (E). It is analyzed below along with reasons:
\textit{Nostoc} belonging to the kingdom Monera (E) are unicellular, filamentous and colonial. Cells contain chromatin material but no nucleolus and nuclear membrane. That is, the nucleus is not well organized. Also, plastids, mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum are absent in their cells and cells divide by mitosis. They mainly consume food by absorption method.
On the other hand, diatoms belonging to the kingdom Protista (F) are unicellular or multicellular, single or colonial and have a well-structured nucleus. In their cells, the chromatin material is surrounded by a nuclear membrane. Apart from having all types of organelles, they are capable of asexual reproduction through mitosis and sexual reproduction through conjugation. Also, the organisms of Protista kingdom consume food by photosynthetic or absorptive method.
So, the comparative discussion of the above characteristics shows that the characteristics of diatoms (Figure-F) are similar to those of higher organisms which are not observed in case of \textit{Nostoc} (Figure-E). So, between diatoms and \textit{Nostoc}, diatoms (Figure-F) are more advanced.","image":null,"image_url":null}]

A comparative discussion based on their evolutionary development is given below:
Life on earth has evolved progressively from simple to complex forms. In the initial stages, organisms were simple, unicellular, and prokaryotic. Over time, through evolution, organisms became increasingly complex. Characteristics such as the structure and number of cells, mode of nutrition, reproduction, movement, etc., have become more organized and advanced from one one kingdom to the next.
Specimen A is \textit{Oryza sativa} or rice. It belongs to the Plantae kingdom. Advanced tissue systems are present in its body. It produces embryos and undergoes anisogamous sexual reproduction. It is a flowering plant.
Specimen B is \textit{Tenualosailisha} or hilsa fish. It belongs to the Animalia kingdom. It is multi-cellular and possesses complex tissue systems. It ingests food. During embryonic development, embryonic layers are formed.
In conclusion, analyzing the characteristics of these two organisms reveals that organisms of the Animalia kingdom (B) are evolutionarily more developed and more advanced in terms of their characteristics than those of the Plantae kingdom (A).","image":null,"image_url":null}]

Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"'C' in the stem is water lily. Its scientific name is \textit{Nymphaea nouchali}. This plant has been named according to the naming system given by Carolus Linnaeus and approved by ICBN. The process is given below:
i. In the naming of water lily, Latin words or Latin words in English should be used.
ii. Here, \textit{Nymphaea} is genus name and \textit{nouchali} is the name of the species.
iii. It is a unique name because a same legitimate name cannot be used for naming two distinct organisms.
iv. The first alphabet of the first name would be in capital letter with the remaining alphabets in small letter. For example, N should be capital and the rest of the alphabets will be in small letter.
v. At the time of printing of a scientific name, it should be written in italics. For example: \textit{Nymphaea nouchali}.
vi. When a scientific name is handwritten, its two parts should be separately underlined. For example: \underline{Nymphaea}\ \underline{nouchali}.
vii. The scientist who gives the scientific name of an organism can have his/her name cited in abbreviated form at the end of binomial name along with the year of naming. For example: \textit{Nymphaea nouchali} L. (Here, L is the short form of Linnaeus).","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"Which one is superior between stem 'A' and 'B'? Evaluate after comparative discussion between the kingdoms.","marks":4,"answer":"A and B of the stem are diatom and blue green algae. Blue green algae belongs to Kingdom-1, Monera and diatom belongs to Kingom-2, Protista. The comparative analysis between the two is given below:
i. Blue green algae is usually unicellular, filamentous. On the otherhand, diatom is unicellular, colonial or filamentous.
ii. The nucleus of blue green algae is not well constructed. There is chromatin material in the cell but no nucleolus or nuclear membrane. On the otherhand, diatom has well constructed nucleus. There is DNA, RNA and protein in the chromatin materials.
iii. In the cell of blue green algae, there is so plastid, mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum but ribosomes. On the other hand, in diatom there all these are present.
iv. The main way of food intake in blue green algae is absorption but some of them produce food through photosynthesis. On the otherhand, diatom takes food by absorption or photosynthesis.
v. In blue green algae, the cell divides through a process of binary fission. On the other hand, in diatom, asexual and sexual reproduction occurs through mitosis and conjugation.
From the above comparison, it can be stated that diatom is more developed than blue green algae.","image":null,"image_url":null}]

Their cells contain nuclear materials covered by a nuclear membrane. In the chromatin material, there are DNA, RNA and protein. All types of cell organelles are present. As the organisms of kingdom Protista have the characteristics of eukaryotes, they are called eukaryata.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"The organisms of kingdom 'P' and 'Q' are of different characteristics-Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"Kingdom 'P' and 'Q' mentioned in the stem are kingdom Fungi (P) and kingdom Animalia (Q) respectively. Their characteristics are different from each other. This is explained below-
In case of kingdom Fungi (P), most of organisms are terrestrial, saprophytic or parasitic. Single cell or mycelium constitute their body. They have well-organized nucleus in their cell. They do not have any chloroplast and thus cannot make food on their own. They get nutrition by means of absorption. They reproduce by haploid spores and their cells divide by means of mitosis.
On the other hand, organisms of kingdom Animalia (Q) are eukaryotic and multicellular animals. Their cells do not have non-living cell walls, plastids or vacuoles in them. Because of no plastids in their cells, they are heterotrophs, and so they depend on other organisms for their food. After ingestion, they digest their food. They have advanced and complex tissue systems. Sexual reproduction is their usual way of reproduction. Haploid gametes are usually produced in the reproductive organs of mature and diploid males and females. Embryonic layers are developed at the time of their embryonic development.
So, from the discussion stated above, we can say that the characteristics of kingdom Fungi and kingdom Animalia are different from each other.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"In the classification of the stem the gradual structural development of organism from simple to complex has occurred Analyze.","marks":4,"answer":"R. H. Whittaker in 1969 first proposed the five kingdom classification of the living organisms. Later, in 1974, Margulis placed these five kingdoms in two Super kingdoms. These are Prokaryota and Eukaryota. She placed only one kingdom 1. Monera in the super kingdom Prokaryota and four kingdoms 2. Protista, 3. Fungi, 4. Plantae and 5. Animalia in the super kingdom Eukaryota. When the features of the organisms are considered, it will be found that organisms of the kingdom:
Monera- are simple, unicellular or multicellular and microscopic with nucleus having no well organised membrane.
As we proceed, we will find that the organisms gradually develop into complex to very complex structures. The characteristics and number of cells, structure of the body, nature of food habit, movement etc. of the organisms included in one kingdom are developed in a more organised and improved way in the next kingdom.
The nucleus of the organisms of the kingdom 1. Monera is not well organised and most of the organisms in this kingdom are unicellular. But the organisms of Eukaryota of the kingdoms are multicellular and their cells have well organised nucleus and most of the organisms in this kingdom are unicellular.
The organisms of kingdom 2 (Protista) and 3 (Fungi) have no tissue differentiation but organisms of kingdom 4 (Plantae) and 5 (Animalia) have well organized tissue system in the body.
The organisms included in kingdoms 1 to 4 take their food by absorption and can not engulf their food but the organisms of kingdom 5 (Animalia) engulf their food. Moreover, the organism of kingdom 5 (Animalia) has the capacity of locomotion which is generally absent in the other kingdoms.
Considering all these features, it may be concluded that the gradual structural development of organisms from simple to complex has occurred and the classification of the living world into five kingdoms and their arrangement hierarchically is justified and scientific.","image":null,"image_url":null}]
